 Follow Us On: News Movies Bollywood Ramayana: Why Yash's Ravana feels more authentic in Kannada than in Hindi Ramayana: Why Yash's Ravana feels more authentic in Kannada than in Hindi
 Yash's Ravana feels more authentic in Kannada, where his voice, pauses and signature swagger add another layer to the performance. Sharad Kelkar impresses in Hindi, but some things are hard to replicate.
 Advertisement Yash’s Ravana feels more authentic in Kannada, despite Sharad Kelkar’s strong Hindi dubbing (Photo edit: Sanjay Ponnappa/India Today) By: Sanjay Ponnappa Bengaluru , Nov 15, 2026 11:37 IST Last Updated Nov 15, 2026 11:37 IST Published by Sanjay Ponnappa CS Nov 15, 2026 11:37 IST For Yash, the voice is as much a part of the persona as the attitude, swagger and screen presence. And nowhere is that more evident than in his Kannada portrayal of Ravana in Ramayana: Part 1 . While his performance is impressive irrespective of the language, there is something undeniably more authentic about watching him bring Ravana to life in his mother tongue, even if it is Brahma AI doing the lip-sync.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story For an actor whose screen persona has been built as much on his voice as his physical presence, this difference is hard to miss.
 Yash has voiced his dialogues in the Kannada version of Nitesh Tiwari's ambitious adaptation of the epic. His peculiar voice, measured pauses, distinct intonation and the attitude with which he delivers his lines come together beautifully. The Kannada dialogues are no less powerful than their Hindi counterparts. They don't feel like a dubbed version struggling to retain the weight of the original. Instead, they have a rhythm and cultural familiarity that complement Yash 's and everybody else's performances.
 And with Yash playing Ravana, those dialogues land several times harder.
 The much-discussed ten-heads-of-Ravana sequence, in particular, is several times more impactful in Kannada. The shifts in tone, the authority in his voice and the subtle variations in his delivery, matching the various shades of Ravana, make the scene considerably more immersive. It is in moments like these that Yash's voice becomes an extension of his performance rather than just a means of delivering dialogue.
 There is also a fascinating legacy angle to this performance. Several viewers have drawn comparisons between Yash's Ravana and the legendary Dr Rajkumar, one of Kannada cinema 's most celebrated performers of mythological and historical characters. Rajkumar famously played Ravana in the 1958 Kannada film Bhookailasa , bringing considerable gravitas to the character. 
 An X post with an AI generated image showing Dr Rajkumar handing over the responsibility of carrying Kannada cinema's legacy forward to Yash 
 Watching Yash command the screen in a similar mythological setting has prompted comparisons that feel like an acknowledgement of a legacy being carried forward. It is not necessarily about recreating Rajkumar's performance, but about seeing another Kannada superstar bring his own interpretation to an iconic character.
 The Hindi version, meanwhile, has Sharad Kelkar, known for his dubbing work in films such as Baahubali and Salaar , lending his voice to Yash. The decision followed criticism of Yash's Hindi dialogue delivery and pronunciation in the film's trailer. Kelkar brings his trademark baritone and gravitas to Ravana, making it a genuinely impressive dubbing performance.
 Speaking exclusively to Variety, Kelkar had nothing but praise for Yash. "Yash has given an outstanding performance. He is the best choice for the role and he understood the character perfectly. Dubbing for him was not at all easy," he said. He explained that although Yash speaks Hindi well, his Kannada-speaking background influences his accent and rhythm with Hindi words. The team eventually felt his voice needed to be dubbed for the Hindi version. Kelkar also specifically praised Yash's Kannada performance, calling his voice fantastic.
 advertisement However, for fans and admirers who have followed Yash through his Kannada films , the difference is unmistakable. This is not a criticism of Kelkar's work. Rather, it highlights how closely Yash's voice, mannerisms and performance are intertwined. His voice is an integral part of the 'Rocking Star Yash' persona. When he speaks, the attitude, pauses and variations are as recognisable as his expressions.
 Interestingly, the difference is less pronounced with Ranbir Kapoor's Lord Rama. The Kannada voice used for Ranbir feels closer to his familiar vocal texture and does not stand out as a distinctly different voice. While the Hindi original is more effective in his case, the transition is not as noticeable as it is with Yash.
 Ultimately, both versions have their merits. Kelkar's voice gives Ravana considerable weight in Hindi. But the Kannada version offers something more personal: Yash without a vocal intermediary. For audiences who know the actor beyond KGF , that connection makes all the difference.
 A great dubbing artist can recreate the power of a performance. But sometimes, authenticity is impossible to replicate. - Ends ALSO READ | Ramayana's Karnataka takeover: Rs 100 crore in 9 days and how Yash rewrites history MUST WATCH:
